requirements.note: Inset-grouped Lists screen with Today (21) and All (135) at the top, then six coloured lists with open counts. Counts update after completing, adding and deleting.

Open tasks come first, then a 'Completed (9)' header that collapses and expands, with its state exposed to accessibility. Tapping the circle completes a task and moves it into Completed; the menu also offers 'Hide Completed'.

The New Task sheet has title (focused on open), notes, a Due Date switch that reveals an inline graphical calendar, Priority and List pull-down menus, and Add is disabled until there is a title. Tapping a task opens a matching Details sheet; title, date and priority edits were saved.
Overdue dates show a red '! Overdue · Sat, Oct 17'. High priority shows an orange '!!!' and an orange checkbox ring.

Swipe to delete is the system swipe action (trash icon) and works. Reorder is only available after More > Edit Tasks, which shows system grabbers. The drag saves the correct order, but the list then shows the wrong rows: one task appeared twice and another vanished. This happened twice, and the screen stayed wrong until the app was relaunched.

'Add List' opens an alert with a text field. Swiping a list row offers Rename (alert with a clear button) and Delete; deleting a list that has tasks asks for confirmation and gives the task count. Rename and Delete are also in the list's More menu.
Completions, edits, added and deleted tasks, the new order, and created, renamed and deleted lists all survived relaunching.

bugs: After reordering by drag in Edit Tasks, the list shows stale rows: one task appears twice and another disappears until the app is relaunched. The saved order is correct. Reproduced twice.
A newly created list is added to the bottom of My Lists while the built-in lists are in alphabetical order, so the order is inconsistent.
tells: The task checkbox buttons are announced as 'Circle' or 'selected' instead of 'Complete <task>'. The cell labels are good.
Reordering is hidden behind More > Edit Tasks; there is no long-press-to-drag on rows.
At the largest text size, notes in the list truncate ('See the email fro…'), and the huge bottom 'New Task' toolbar button covers the rows.
The 'New Task' plus glyph is drawn black or white instead of in the tint colour; only the label is tinted.
A.scroll: The All list (about 135 rows) scrolls smoothly on slow drags and flings, with no blank or late-appearing rows. It has a proper blurred scroll-edge under the nav bar, the large title collapses correctly, and it rubber-bands past the top.

requirements.note: Inset-grouped Lists screen with Today (21) and All (135), then the six lists with counts, kept in data order. The lists have no icons or colours. Counts update correctly.

Open tasks come first, then a 'Completed · 10' header with a chevron that collapses and expands the section. Tapping the circle completes or reopens a task (switch labelled 'Complete <title>' / 'Reopen <title>').

The New Task sheet has a focused title field, notes, a Due Date switch with a compact date picker, Priority and List menus, and Add is disabled until there is a title. Tapping a task opens Details with a checkmark Save; title, date and priority edits were saved.
Overdue dates show a red '! Overdue · Oct 17, 2026'. High priority shows a red '!!!'; low and medium show grey '!' and '!!'.
Every row has a grab handle that reorders by drag directly, and the new order shows at once and persists. Swiping left shows a Delete button that works.

The + button opens a New List sheet. Touch and hold opens a context menu with Rename (a sheet) and Delete. Rows also swipe to Delete, and deleting always asks for confirmation ('This deletes the list and all of its tasks').
Completion, edits, reorder, list creation, rename and deletion all survived relaunching.

tells: Weak scroll-edge effect: once the large title collapses, rows slide under the inline title and toolbar buttons and visibly overlap 'Trip' or 'All' instead of passing under a blurred bar.
Permanent drag grabbers on every task row, which is not how iOS lists show reordering (Reminders hides them; system lists show them only in edit mode).
The swipe Delete action is a short text-only pill that does not fill the row height.
The Due Date switch and the Completed header have no accessibility label or button trait (the header is a plain element with no expanded or collapsed state).
The rename list field has no clear button, and renaming is discoverable only through a 'Touch and hold' footer hint.
The checkbox circles stay small at the largest text size, and the edit sheet's title truncates on one line ('Write the plu…').
My Lists rows have no icons or colours, so the screen looks plainer than Reminders.
B.scroll: The All list (grouped by list) scrolls smoothly on drags and flings, with no blank rows. Scroll position is kept after opening and closing a task. The only flaw is content showing through the nav bar's weak edge effect.

why: Both cover the whole spec and persist everything. B's drag-to-reorder works directly and correctly, while A's reorder sits behind Edit Tasks and leaves duplicated or missing rows on screen until relaunch. A looks and behaves more like a hand-built iOS app: system swipe actions, a proper scroll-edge blur, coloured list icons and a native inline calendar. B has rows overlapping the nav title, permanent grabbers and hand-drawn swipe buttons. On balance A is closer to shippable, though its reorder display bug is the most serious single defect in either app.
